newsitem.title: USA: Dow Jones heir wants Murphy as CEO -- CNBC.
newsitem.headline: Dow Jones heir wants Murphy as CEO -- CNBC.

text.p: William Cox III, a member of the family that controls Dow Jones & Co Inc, would like Thomas Murphy, a former chief executive of Capital Cities/ABC Inc, to take over as chief executive of Dow Jones, according to an interview aired on CNBC business television on Monday.

Cox and fellow dissident shareholder Elisabeth Goth met with financier Warren Buffett last May to discuss their desire to improve shareholder value at Dow Jones, Cox told CNBC. Buffett recommended outside directors be named to the Dow Jones board and that Murphy be placed as chief executive, according to the interview.
Cox and Goth then met with Murphy in November, CNBC said.
In a statement released through Capital Cities/ABC, Murphy acknowledged the meeting with the Dow Jones heirs but said he "mostly listened" during the session.
He said he had not met with the Dow Jones heirs since then and had "no plans to return to work."
Murphy, 71, retired from Capital Cities/ABC after its 1995 merger with the Walt Disney Co and now sits on the Disney board.

A Dow Jones spokesman said the company was "not looking for a new CEO." The spokesman said Cox did not represent the views of the Bancroft family, which owns less than 50 percent of Dow Jones' common stock, though almost 70 percent voting control in the company.
Cox, who resigned from Dow Jones last month, said in the interview he was not giving up his efforts to boost shareholder value.
